info.label: Elektra
info.desc: "Metallica", commonly known as "The Black Album", is the fifth studio album by the American heavy metal band Metallica, released on August 12, 1991, by Elektra Records. Recording took place at One on One Recording Studios in Los Angeles over an eight-month period, during which the band frequently clashed with producer Bob Rock. The album represented a stylistic shift for Metallica, moving away from the thrash metal sound of their first four albums towards a slower, heavier, and more polished approach. To promote the album, Metallica embarked on an extensive touring schedule and released five singles: "Enter Sandman", "The Unforgiven", .
info.producers: Bob Rock, James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich

podcast.body: Bob Rock, the producer, sold his stake in Metallica's Black Album, indicating the significant and ongoing royalty income generated by such major releases for producers. "Bob Rock, for example, sold his stake in Metallica's black album. He was getting royalties from that and he sold them."

podcast.body: Prior to Bob Rock's involvement, Metallica was a "big cult band" selling around two million copies per record. Rock convinced them to streamline their sound by focusing on traditional song structures, melody, and pulling back on riffing, drumming, and thrashing. This change, while initially disliked by purists, propelled the band from selling two million to twenty million records, making it a major commercial and critical breakthrough. "But the band went from selling two million records to twenty million records."

podcast.body: Released in 1991, this album received a double diamond award, with the band claiming sales of 30 million, though it is confirmed to have sold at least 22 million copies. Metallica is described as part of the "old breed" of diamond record artists, a sales achievement that is now rare. "Patalica, who have a double diamond award for their Black Album from 1991. They claim sales of 30 million, which might be a bit inflated, but we know for sure that it has sold at least 22 million."

podcast.body: Released in the summer of 1991, "The Black Album" marked a significant shift for Metallica. Produced by Canadian super producer Bob Rock, it saw the band's sound slow down and become more polished, moving away from their previous raw speed and power. Despite purist objections, it sold over 15 million copies, a "huge breakthrough" that introduced Metallica to a wider audience and repositioned the band as music for outsiders and misfits, aligning them with an "alternative" identity. "Metallica released their famous black album... Bob Rock got them to slow down a bit and polished up their sound."
